A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP-IN study, despite v4's VITRIX-CLIPIN title. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The separately titled supplement in v2 largely duplicates material retained elsewhere.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, retrieval, fine-grained perception, compositional reasoning, MLLM, and ablation results.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and reports additional robustness evaluations, compositional comparisons, and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same hard-negative construction, symmetric loss, RoPE distillation, and joint short-caption/long-caption training objective. The added alternative encoders and losses are experimental comparators, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v4 adds ARO evaluation and ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch, and ImageNet-V2 tests, substantially extending coverage to adversarial examples, artistic renditions, sketches, and distribution shift. Earlier benchmarks remain represented. The additional 30-million-caption experiment changes training scale without identifying a new training domain.

E2.justification: v4 adds direct comparisons against NegCLIP and Triplet loss variants in Table 10 and a LongCLIP-initialized alternative in Table 8. SigLIP2 also joins the compositional comparison in Table 3, where v2 compared only OpenAI CLIP. These substantively extend comparisons of the central design choices.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a 30-million-caption training condition, controlled encoder and loss alternatives, and additional backbone/resolution configurations for compositional evaluation. Table 3 adds Winoground averages and directional SPEC metrics. The main training settings in Section 4.1 remain unchanged; these are additional experimental settings.

E4.justification: v4 adds RoPE-versus-interpolation and symmetric-loss-versus-alternative-loss ablations, ImageNet distribution-shift tests, and an 18M-versus-30M caption-scale analysis. Table 11 extends long-caption removal analysis to MMVP and long-text retrieval. The earlier data-source ablations and feature visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The additional experiments do not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Expanded Table 3 and new Tables 8–12 add substantial results. For ViT-L/14 at 336 resolution, CLIP-IN's Winoground text/image scores change from 35.5/13.5 to 33.0/11.8, and SugarCrepe changes from 79.4 to 77.2; the corresponding CLIP SugarCrepe score changes from 73.8 to 74.8. Table 1 changes the 224-resolution ShareGPT4V text-to-image score from 91.1 to 91.9. The new 30M-caption condition reports 85.1 long-caption retrieval and 76.2 ImageNet accuracy, versus 76.4 and 77.0 for the retained 18M condition.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–8 are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems, proofs, formal assumptions, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about instruction-editing negatives, complementary long captions, RoPE adaptation, fine-grained perception, and MLLM benefits. The title change and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 supplements the retained synergy explanation with comparative interpretations favoring RoPE and symmetric loss, a stronger statement that long captions are necessary, and discussion of closing the FG-CLIP retrieval gap through caption scaling. Appendix A adds interpretations about artistic and sketch generalization. Some claims of consistent improvement exceed the mixed findings in Tables 3 and 9.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project-access link in the abstract. Conversely, Section 4.2 omits v2's explicit Flickr30K 1K and COCO 5K test-image counts, without stating revised splits. The main hardware, optimizer, learning rate, loss weights, and batch-size disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Four references supporting the new ImageNet-variant evaluations are added: works on robustness, natural adversarial examples, ImageNet generalization, and sketch representations. The existing related-work discussion and central positioning against prior CLIP methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 consolidates v2's duplicated appendices and separately titled supplement into one A–E appendix structure. Compositional evaluation is merged into Section 4.3, benchmark descriptions move to Appendix C, and the compositional-results narrative is rewritten. The title and author information also change, while most methodological prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 expands from two rows to eight with additional grouped metric columns, and Tables 8–12 introduce new displays. Duplicate supplementary tables and figures are consolidated. The existing feature visualizations and editing examples are reordered and renumbered, while the framework diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: The added loss and encoder comparisons, robustness tests, and caption-scale analysis improve empirical scrutiny of design choices that v2 left less directly tested. However, v4 introduces reporting inconsistencies: the discussion retains obsolete SugarCrepe/SPEC values and claims ARO improvement at 336 resolution although Table 3 shows 60.7 versus CLIP's 61.0. The added evidence provides a net benefit, but these inconsistencies limit the overall gain.
